title: Eulogy & Epitaph Writing
opening: Name a quality or contribution you want your life to express. Then compare it with one present choice and the pattern you want to avoid.

labels.comparison: From imagined remembrance to present conduct
labels.comparisonIntro: Imagine a teacher who wants to help people think independently. They write a moving account of that contribution, but usually answer every question before a learner can try. Examine the connection before deciding what to change.
labels.adherenceText: Helping people think independently is the desired contribution. Writing that wish does not show that the current teaching method supports it.
labels.valueText: Giving an answer before the learner can try may keep them dependent. Look at the actual interaction; desired praise is not evidence of the contribution.
labels.outcomeText: For one suitable question, let the learner try, ask what they noticed, and offer help where needed. Check whether the interaction supports more independent thinking; one attempt does not prove a lasting result.
labels.signalQuestion: Choose a part of the comparison
labels.rhythmText: The source uses imagined remembrance and an ending to avoid. Use that perspective only if it is suitable for you. A review of a valued year or week can reveal the same priorities without a death-related frame. Everyday relationships and present life matter; the exercise does not require a grand legacy.
labels.practice: Connect a desired quality with a present choice
labels.practiceIntro: Choose the horizon that helps you reflect. Add only the notes that are useful; blank fields are fine. Keep the desired contribution, unwanted pattern and current evidence distinct.

example.contribution: Support learners in finding and explaining an answer themselves.
example.avoid: Being praised as indispensable while people depend on my answers.
example.present: This week, I often answer before a learner has tried the question.
example.connection: The learner has little chance to show what they can do without me.
example.change: Offer one suitable question, let the learner try, then ask what they noticed before giving help.
